sources.title: Models | Aion Labs Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27. Exact aion-labs/aion-3.0-mini entry describes collaborative generation by multiple specialized DeepSeek-family models, but names no component checkpoint and publishes no nominal total or active count. The explicit DeepSeek V3.2 variant statement elsewhere on this page belongs to Aion 2.0, not Aion 3.0 Mini. Release remains 2026-05-14, with 128K context and reasoning.

sources.title: Aion Labs public models API
sources.evidence: Fetched the exact entry again on 2026-10-27. It describes a collaborative multi-model DeepSeek-family system without component identities, counts or activation details. The architecture object contains only text->text modality. It confirms 2026-05-14, 131072 context, reasoning and tools; replacement_model_id is null.

sources.title: API Reference | Aion Labs Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27. Documents model-discovery and capability fields and Aion 3.0 Mini reasoning_effort levels none, low, medium, high and max, default medium. The per-model parameter capabilities heading means API request controls, not learned-weight counts; no total or active count or named component lineage is disclosed.

sources.title: Terms of Service of the Aion Labs API, version 2026-10-17
sources.evidence: Defines Models by the official Models page. Section 6 reserves service/software property to Aion Labs or licensors and grants no rights in Models beyond service use. It is an API service agreement, not a downloadable weight license.

sources.title: Models.dev Aion-3.0-Mini record
sources.evidence: Baseline provenance: generic efficiency/automation description, closed weights, 2026-05-14 date, text modalities, reasoning, tools, and 131072 context. Its comment attributes the date to the official API.

sources.title: Aion-3.0-Mini - API Pricing & Providers
sources.evidence: Reopened 2026-10-27. Exact ID is described as a DeepSeek-family collaborative system, with no named base checkpoint or parameter count. Its related-model section attaches a 32B claim to the distinct Aion-1.0-Mini; that count is not evidence for Aion-3.0-Mini. Reports July 7, 2026 as Released, conflicting with the original developer date. Used for corroboration and disambiguation, not as a developer count specification.

sources.title: OpenRouter exact Aion 3.0 Mini endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Fetched 2026-10-27. The exact ID resolves to an AionLabs endpoint named aion-labs/aion-3.0-mini-20260707. Its metadata repeats the DeepSeek-family multi-model description; architecture lists modality and tokenizer, not dense/MoE structure. No total or active count or named checkpoint appears. This serving-provider record corroborates identity but adds no parameter evidence.

name.note: Same exact identifier; Aion Labs styles the name Aion 3.0 Mini, while the serving provider uses Aion-3.0-Mini.

developer.note: Official developer documentation and service brand establish Aion Labs.

family.note: Explicitly built on the DeepSeek family. The particular component checkpoints are not named.

release_date.note: Developer documentation and API agree on May 14. OpenRouter reports July 7; retain the original developer date and record this discrepancy.

open_weights.note: Published as a hosted service; the applicable terms grant only service use of the listed Models. No weight release is identified in the reviewed official material.

license.note: No separate model/weight license identified. API use is governed by the Aion Labs service terms.

parameters_b.note: Fresh developer documentation and API review finds no published nominal total or identified component count. Only DeepSeek-family lineage is stated; no named-base relationship supports nominal inheritance. Aion 2.0's DeepSeek V3.2 lineage and Aion 1.0 Mini's 32B size belong to different models. Targeted searches for newer developer disclosures found no supported count for this exact ID.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-parameter specification, component activation count or phase-dependent count is published for this exact collaborative system. Component checkpoints and neural architectures are unnamed, so neither a DeepSeek-family active count nor a dense-model convention can be applied. API reasoning controls do not disclose parameter activation.

architecture.note: Collaborative multi-model generation is disclosed, but underlying neural architecture and component topology are not. The API architecture object describes modality only; dense or MoE cannot be assigned.

context_window.note: Exact context_length from the developer endpoint, in tokens.

reasoning.note: The model reports reasoning=true; the documentation specifies its reasoning controls.

tool_call.note: The exact model entry reports tool_calls=true, defined as accepting tools and returning tool calls.

description.value: DeepSeek-based collaborative multi-model system for narrative generation and storytelling
description.note: Replaces unsupported efficiency, latency, extraction and automation positioning with the developer-described design and narrative focus.

patch.description: DeepSeek-based collaborative multi-model system for narrative generation and storytelling
patch.notes: Aion Labs identifies multiple collaborating DeepSeek-family models but names no component checkpoints and publishes no total or active parameter counts. Neural architecture remains undisclosed. Its official release date is 2026-05-14; OpenRouter lists 2026-07-07.

summary: Re-audited parameters on 2026-10-27 against current developer model documentation, the exact public API entry, API reference and serving-provider metadata, with targeted searches for newer disclosures. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed: the developer names only the DeepSeek family, not a base checkpoint or sized component. No sibling-model size is transferred and no component or phase count is invented. Existing DeepSeek-family description, capabilities, unknown neural architecture and developer/provider release-date discrepancy are preserved.
